<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Vaughan via the Tether prime (pij-causal-salamander), brief tether-governance/.harness/government/briefs/xgov-pij-watchdog-start.md. A stream seat that acks its brief and then idles is caught only by --every, so primes arm `--every 2m` at spawn and rely on the seat re-arming itself `--every 20m` after its first report; the seat forgetting is the failure. `--start <dur>` makes the first check short and switches to `--every` by itself.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- `pij watchdog on [<seat>] --start <dur> [--every <dur>]` arms a short first stall check that hands over to --every with no second call.
- `--every` alone behaves exactly as today.
- `pij watchdog status` shows both intervals and which phase is active.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Changing when a seat counts as stalled (working or parked seats stay silent; the plan-178 answered-nudge brake stays).
- PA watchdog behaviour.
- Deploying the daemon (a separate, owner-coordinated bounce).

<a id="risks-assumptions"></a>

## Risks & Assumptions

last_event_at counts every spine event for the seat, including watchdog.on and watchdog.nudge, so it cannot mark the first report; the edge reads the latest `report.now` (CARD_EVENT_KIND) via spine.latest_matching, as the PA path does. A daemon restart loses the in-memory nudged map; started_at is persisted, so the start phase never repeats.
